statement: On a number line, Kit starts at 8 and jumps 3 steps to the left, one step at a time. Where does Kit land?

choices.misconception: I gave the number of steps instead of the place where Kit lands.
I counted 8 as my first step, so I said 8, 7, 6.
I jumped to the right and counted 8 as my first step, so I said 8, 9, 10.
I jumped to the right, where the numbers get bigger, instead of to the left.

hints: Which way do numbers get smaller on a number line?
Numbers get smaller as you go left. Draw the line, put your finger on 8, and count only the jumps you make, not the place where you start.
From 8, the first jump lands on 7, the second on 6 and the third on one more number to the left.

solutions.reliable: Going left on a number line makes numbers smaller. From 8, one step lands on 7, two steps on 6 and three steps on 5. Kit lands on 5. The idea to keep: count the jumps, not the number you start on.
solutions.elegant: Three steps to the left is the same as taking 3 away, and 8 take away 3 is 5. The idea to keep: moving left is subtracting.

whyOnTest: Number line jumps test direction and the classic slip of counting the starting point as a step.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
